verification_report.summary: The strict open-domain arguments, including rational-centred traces, algebraically closed base change, finite-flat continuous trace, arbitrary-field disc constancy, exact fibre slicing, strict-open annulus affinity, and strict-open polycylinder joint affinity, pass sequential and reference checks. The package nevertheless fails the strict criterion because its endpoint extension is not proved: the final theorem uses a false description of Berkovich absolute analytic interior, and the annulus proof omits the endpoint residue-branch argument. All cited external results were found and were applicable; they do not repair these endpoint defects.

critical_errors.location: Proof of Theorem thm:p062-arbitrary-field-polycylinder-candidate, final endpoint paragraph
critical_errors.issue: The assertion that the absolute analytic interior of a closed or half-closed standard polycylinder 'is the corresponding open polycylinder' is false. Already for a strict closed Berkovich disc, the absolute interior is the closed disc minus its Gauss boundary point, and it contains open residue branches centered at points of boundary modulus; it is strictly larger than {|T|<R}. Consequently the coordinatewise strict open polycylinder is not dense in the whole closed/half-closed domain, and applying only the open theorem there plus continuity does not prove the endpoint assertion.

gaps.location: Proof of Proposition prop:p062-arbitrary-field-annulus-candidate, final endpoint sentence
gaps.issue: The open-annulus proof does not by itself prove the closed and half-closed variants. The absolute analytic interior of a strict closed annulus is not the coordinatewise strict annulus r<|T|<R: it also contains the residue-disc branches at the endpoint radii (only the analytic boundary Gauss points are omitted). The strict annulus is not dense in those endpoint branches, so the sentence 'Restriction to the absolute interior and continuity' skips the argument identifying h on those branches with the limiting affine skeleton value. One must apply the disc theorem on every endpoint branch or rerun the polynomial-trace comparison for rigid endpoint points, then glue through the endpoint Gauss point by continuity and invoke rigid density.

repair_hints: First replace the false claim that absolute analytic interior equals the coordinatewise strict polycylinder. For each closed or half-closed annulus, prove the affine formula on every endpoint-radius residue-disc branch: either apply the already proved arbitrary-field disc theorem on each branch, or extend the polynomial-tube/finite-trace argument to rigid points with |T| equal to an endpoint; then identify the branch constant with the limiting skeleton value by continuity at the endpoint Gauss point and use rigid density. Next give a coordinatewise endpoint argument for products over arbitrary completed residue fields, covering all boundary strata and showing that successive endpoint replacements preserve h and have the same canonical Gauss endpoint. Only after that may continuity extend the jointly affine logarithmic formula to the whole closed/half-closed polycylinder.
